Thanks — reviewed the PDF and the inventory. A couple technical notes before Marissa schedules the kickoff:

- Redwood private endpoints expect a /29 or larger for control plane allocation (we usually reserve 6 IPs). If Avalon can allocate a /28 that gives some breathing room for staging vs prod.
- For VPC peering: we prefer no overlapping CIDRs. If you must overlap, we can use our NAT + proxy routing pattern but that adds ~90–120s to initial handshakes; not ideal for low-latency use-cases.
- Firewall rules: allow outbound TCP 443 to 34.200.0.0/16 and inbound from our peered VPC ranges on 443 and 50051 (gRPC) during the test window.

If Priya can send the proposed CIDRs and a primary/secondary test host IP, Karthik and I will pre-stage the peering request and a temporary route table to validate.

—Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
